headline.caveat: Contract dollars undisclosed. NVIDIA has booked ~60% of TSMC's 2026 CoWoS advanced-packaging capacity (press/analyst-reported) plus leading-edge wafer supply for Blackwell/Rubin — the single largest customer commitment at TSMC, which guided 2026 capex to $60-64B partly on this demand.

realized_to_date.caveat: NVIDIA pays as wafers/packages deliver, plus capacity prepayments that are aggregated (not itemized) in both firms' disclosures. NVIDIA's data-center COGS implies tens of billions annually to TSMC.

nature_md: The load-bearing supply relationship of the AI buildout: TSMC fabricates effectively all of NVIDIA's leading-edge GPUs and performs CoWoS advanced packaging, with NVIDIA reported to have booked ~60% of TSMC's 2026 CoWoS capacity. Structured as rolling capacity reservations and purchase orders (with prepayments/deposits customary for capacity locks) rather than one disclosed mega-contract. CoWoS capacity — not wafer starts — has repeatedly been the binding constraint on global AI-accelerator output; overflow goes to OSATs like ASE.

accounting.payer_treatment_md: NVIDIA carries supply commitments and capacity prepayments in its inventory-purchase-obligation disclosures (tens of billions across suppliers); wafer/packaging costs flow through COGS as products ship (NVIDIA gross margin ~70%+ prices well above these input costs).
accounting.payee_treatment_md: TSMC recognizes foundry/packaging revenue on delivery — HPC/AI is now the majority of its revenue mix — and is spending $60-64B of 2026 capex to expand CoWoS/leading-edge capacity against these bookings; prepayments sit as contract liabilities until earned.

both_sides_md: **Bull:** capacity pre-booking is rational scarcity management, and TSMC's capex response is demand-verified — its customers prepay. **Bear:** one customer holding ~60% of the critical packaging bottleneck concentrates the entire ecosystem's supply risk (and TSMC's capex bet) on NVIDIA's demand forecast being right.
